title: Wait for It
novel:
Ted returned from summer with a [[tattoo|tattoo]] on his lower back. He [[blamed|blame]] it on a [[reckless|reckless]] night of tequila. At MacLaren's, Robin [[introduced|introduce]] her new boyfriend Gael — a [[laid-back|laid-back]] surfer whose calm [[accent|accent]] filled Ted with [[jealousy|jealousy]].

Barney [[declared|declare]] that Gael was a [[threat|threat]] to their group. "Cool people [[ruin|ruin]] everything," he [[complained|complain]].

Meanwhile, Lily [[hid|hide]] a dark secret: months of [[debt|debt]] from shopping sprees. She [[begged|beg]] Marshall not to open the mail. When he discovered the [[truth|truth]], he [[whispered|whisper]] that they were broke.

Ted decided to [[remove|remove]] the tattoo. The [[embarrassing|embarrassing]] mark [[reminded|remind]] him that summer was over. As autumn leaves fell, some summers left marks that took years to [[fade|fade]].

tattoo.en: a picture drawn on skin with ink

blame.en: to say someone is responsible for bad things

reckless.en: doing things without thinking about danger

introduce.en: to tell someone another person's name

accent.en: the way people speak in an area

jealousy.en: anger when someone has what you want

declare.en: to say something firmly and publicly

complain.en: to say you are not satisfied

embarrassing.en: making you feel shy or ashamed

fade.en: to slowly lose color or disappear
